summary: Midday dedicated capacity sag correlated with background hyperparameter sweep causing autoscaler misclassification
description:
Issue summary:
During the midday window on 2026-03-13 ~11:20-12:05 PDT VetaHealth experienced a sharp throughput sag on their Dedicated cluster (prod-us-west) that manifested as sustained p95/p99 latency growth and an effective loss of two GPU attachments for ~8-12 minute intervals. The symptom set resembles noisy-neighbor GPU shortages rather than a network outage.

Impact:
- Customer reports 30-60% drop in completed inference throughput for critical routes; business-impacting.
- Several long-lived requests hit 5xx when batchers could not attach to GPUs; internal SLO violations.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: rsv-veta-04 (50 GPUs, NGC-backed).
- Region: prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Models in flight: gpt-large-v2 (low-latency route), redwood/biomed-24b (background batch jobs).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic at normal rate to pinned model gpt-large-v2.
2) Internal scheduler launched a scheduled hyperparameter sweep job (internal team) on same reserved cluster beginning 11:18.
3) At 11:22 autoscaler telemetry spiked (IO wait + ephemeral CPU load) and allocator started transiently shrinking pool; new attachments failed or queued.
4) From 11:22-11:30 many short-streams timed out; prefetched KV cache thrashing observed.
5) Autoscaler misclassified the load as a drop in active inference demand and attempted aggressive shrink/eviction during a high-noise IO period, making slot scarcity worse.

Observed behavior (logs/metrics):
- Grafana traces: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cluster/rsv-veta-04?from=2026-03-13T11:10&to=2026-03-13T12:10 (p99 latency spike).
- Allocator logs show repeated "attach timeout" and "gpu-attach-latency=12000ms" for rsv-veta-04.
- Node exporter/IO metrics: nvme_io_wait and dsk_util spiked on 3 nodes at 11:18-11:28.
- Sidecar logs: background sweep processes produced high CPU and sustained NVME checkpoint writes.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should not shrink capacity when attach latencies are high due to IO noise; it should mark nodes as degraded and route/fallback rather than evict or reduce capacity.
- Background batch jobs should be isolated to lower-priority pools or scheduled outside peak windows on dedicated reservations.

Investigation notes / hypothesis:
- Primary hypothesis: background hyperparameter sweep (internal research job) introduced heavy NVMe write pressure and CPU overhead on nodes hosting VetaHealth's reserved pool. This increased GPU attach latency and inflated autoscaler signals (missed heartbeats / delayed attach). The autoscaler treated telemetry gaps as lower utilization and initiated shrink/eviction, creating a feedback loop that reduced available slots and increased request queuing.
- Secondary hypothesis: KV cache growth from mixed workload caused memory pressure, forcing extra page faults and elongating attach times.
- Evidence: correlation between internal sweep job start time and nvme_io_wait spikes; allocator attach errors coincident with autoscaler shrink commands recorded in scheduler audit log.

Immediate mitigation applied (temporary workaround):
- 11:36: Support escalated to SRE to temporarily hold autoscaler decisions for rsv-veta-04 (grace-window 15m) while we assessed.
- 11:40: Paused the internal hyperparameter sweep on nodes in the reservation. NVMe IO normalized by 11:48 and attach latency recovered.
- 11:52: Removed autoscaler hold; verified steady attach success and throughput recovery by 12:05.

Next steps / follow-ups recommended:
- Permanent controls: add scheduling guard that prevents scheduled research/batch sweeps from targeting active customer-dedicated reservations unless explicitly approved.
- Autoscaler change request: add an IO/attach-latency circuit to prevent shrink actions when attach latency > threshold or when NVMe IO is saturated; open RFC with scheduler team. (see linked PRs).
- Improve telemetry: add allocator attach-latency metric to console per-reservation dashboard and an alert that changes autoscaler behavior.
- Customer communication: notify VetaHealth with post-incident summary and confirm if they'd like stricter node isolation or a dedicated maintenance window for internal jobs.

Related artifacts and timestamps:
- Allocator attach traces: s3://redwood-logs/allocator/rsv-veta-04/2026-03-13/attach-trace-11-22.log
- Scheduler audit: https://gitlab.redwood.internal/scheduler/audits/9843
- Incident Slack thread: #support (link: slack://channel?team=redwood&id=support/tx12345)
comments: 2026-03-13 11:30 - Support (Marina Gomez): Customer reported sharp drop in completed requests; collecting traces and elevating to SRE.
2026-03-13 11:36 - SRE (Daniel Chu): Temporarily set autoscaler noop for rsv-veta-04 to stop aggressive shrink while we validate cause.
2026-03-13 11:40 - Research (Priya Nambiar): Confirmed scheduled hyperparameter-sweep job ID 8427 landed on nodes a1-a3 of the reservation; pausing now.
2026-03-13 11:48 - SRE (Daniel Chu): NVMe and attach latency metrics trending back to normal; hold extended 15m while we observe.
2026-03-13 12:10 - Support (Marina Gomez): Customer confirms throughput recovered; advising follow-up RFC on autoscaler behavior.
resolution: workaround_applied - paused internal sweep and temporarily suspended autoscaler shrink; capacity restored. Follow-up RFC/open PRs for autoscaler circuit and scheduling guard created.

RFC for autoscaler: add attach-latency/IO-aware shrink inhibition (owner: Autoscaler team) - due 2026-03-27
Add attach-latency metric and console alert for reservations (owner: Console/Observability) - due 2026-04-02
